records.text: Allie Beth Stuckey accused Owens of using a Kafka-trap tactic like Black Lives Matter: in Stuckey's account, Owens treated pushback as proof critics were paid and denied that they could possibly sincerely disagree, an approach Stuckey called effective but dishonest
records.speaker: Allie Beth Stuckey

appearances.snippet: In 2020, we all became familiarized with the Kafka trap. It's a rhetorical trick wherein you insist that someone's denial of an accusation proves their guilt. You're denying you're a racist because of your white fragility. It's a way to make your arguments irrefutable without ever having to provide evidence. BLM uses this tactic repeatedly, and now Candace has taken a page out of their book. Anyone, including Charlie's own wife, who pushes back against her conspiracies are only doing so because it's a sign up. They're getting paid. It couldn't possibly be that people sincerely disagree with her methods or can disprove her faulty logic. It's an effective, albeit dishonest way to solidify yourself as the only champion of truth now.

verification.notes: The source transcript and current public transcript preserve Owens reading Stuckey's post nearly verbatim: Stuckey defined a Kafka trap, compared the tactic to BLM, accused Owens of treating disagreement as evidence of a psyop or payment, and called the method effective but dishonest. This verifies the attributed accusation and characterization, not the truth of Stuckey's opinion about Owens's methods.

records.text: Allie Beth Stuckey said a late-August invitation from Charlie Kirk for an early-November Alabama campus event showed that part of the tour was assembled at the last minute and that the UVU stop being booked over the summer was not unusual.
records.speaker: Allie Beth Stuckey

appearances.snippet: This is what she tweeted. She said: "The latest claim is that TPUSA must have been in on Charlie's (Charlie Kirk's) murder because the UVU campus stop was approved in July. ... It was not approved in July; it was requested in July. And that's too short of a timeline for an event in September. ... That is not true. Charlie (Charlie Kirk) texted me at the end of August for a campus event in early November. ... That's about two months out. And the reason he didn't specify which campus is because he didn't even know yet. ... He just knew it was going to be in Alabama. So yes: it does seem like part of this year's campus tour was being put together at the last minute, and UVU being booked over the summer isn't actually unusual.

verification.notes: Allie Beth Stuckey's own podcast confirms that Charlie Kirk invited her in late August to a November 3 Alabama campus event before the specific campus was settled, and that in her experience Turning Point campus stops were often organized very late. This verifies her statement and its experiential basis. Her conclusion that the UVU timing was therefore not unusual is an inference from her experience rather than independently documented UVU scheduling evidence.
